description: contracts/sprint-2.md's own CRIT-203 (the weight-0.15 formal grading criterion Phase 3/5 will use for the edge_case_coverage dimension) was NOT touched by this round's FIND-019 fix commit (b0f120fa1 only added a correction paragraph at lines 311-323; the CRIT-203 frontmatter block at lines 31-35 is untouched) and still states: 'steps 7-9 use the existing `buildChildSpec`-based REQ-305 path, requiring step 6 to have genuinely succeeded first; no row anywhere ever claims `status:"active"` for a failed attempt.' Round 12's own FIND-019 text considered CRIT-203 and concluded it was 'unaffected' -- but that reasoning ONLY examined the narrower 'no row ever claims active for a FAILED ATTEMPT' clause (correctly noting the FIND-003 transient-registry case is not a failed attempt, since executeSpawnAttempt resolves status:'active', not 'failed'). It did NOT examine the SEPARATE, independent factual claim in the same sentence -- 'steps 7-9 use the existing buildChildSpec-based REQ-305 path' -- which is a structural claim about which code path handles EACH of steps 7, 8, AND 9, and which the corrected PROP-307c row now explicitly contradicts for step 9 ('Neither step-9 sub-failure uses "the buildChildSpec-based REQ-305 failure path"'). Confirmed against the real code: spawn-orchestrator.mjs's step 9 (lines 695-736) never calls `buildChildSpec` at all -- it calls `appendChild` directly (line 698) for the ledger row, then `appendCitizenRecord` (line 711, wrapped in try/catch) for the registry side, falling back to `pending-registry-append.js`'s queue on failure. This makes CRIT-203's own passThreshold ('An integration test triggering a failure at each of the 9 steps against a real ledger.js file confirms the above ... FAIL if any step's failure produces no row') actively hazardous if applied literally: injecting a failure at step 9's raw-ledger-append sub-case genuinely produces NO row at all (confirmed passing test at spawn-orchestrator.test.mjs:287-304, which asserts the call rejects rather than resolving with any row) -- exactly the condition CRIT-203's own passThreshold says must FAIL. A literal, mechanical application of CRIT-203 as currently worded would therefore incorrectly grade a FAIL against this genuinely correct, intended, already-implemented-and-tested behavior. CRIT-203 needs the same steps-7-8/step-9 carve-out FIND-019 already applied to PROP-307c.

evidence.snippet: description: A failure injected at each of REQ-307's 9 canonical steps in turn is recorded correctly ... steps 7-9 use the existing `buildChildSpec`-based REQ-305 path, requiring step 6 to have genuinely succeeded first; no row anywhere ever claims `status:"active"` for a failed attempt ... | passThreshold: An integration test triggering a failure at each of the 9 steps against a real `ledger.js` file confirms the above ... FAIL if any step's failure produces no row, a wrongly-shaped row, or a row misread by the sprint-1 aggregation functions.
